描述_ZN: Han Ximeng's Song and Yuan Masterpieces - Washing a Horse, Ming Chongzhen, 33.4 cm in length and 24.5 cm in width.　　The picture is embroidered on a white plain satin ground, with a weeping willow swaying and a horseman under a tree brushing a white black-spotted horse, which is excitedly neighing in the waves of water. The majestic white horse is realistically embroidered with Gu embroidery's best technique of brio and needle, following the texture of its muscles. The spots on the white horse's body are embroidered exactly as the dots in the painting, and although the black embroidery thread has fallen off, the stitching is still vaguely recognizable. In addition, the embroidery is also rendered with brushes in many places, and this "half-painting, half-embroidery" technique is the most basic feature of Gu embroidery, with embroidery as the main focus and supplemented by painting.　　This is a realistic and vivid image of a horse washing, with a light and elegant color scheme, reflecting the characteristics of Gu embroidery's light color rendering. On the opposite page, Dong Qichang inscribed the picture with the following praise: "A jan is concealed in the sky, and the hairy dragon is a bath. The wind is so strong that it can be seen in nine directions. It stands out for its power and wonder, which cannot be restrained. Chasing the clouds by electricity, it is in sight."　　This is one of the masterpieces of Han Ximeng's embroidery "Han Ximeng's Song and Yuan Masterpieces Book" of the Ming Dynasty, with 8 pieces in total.
